https://nineoclock.ro/sameday-announces-.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Bucharest, August 4, 2026 – SAMEDAY confirms the acquisition of 100% of Cargus’ share capital. Following clearance from the Romanian Competition Council, the transaction has been completed, and as of August 3, 2026, Cargus is wholly owned by SAMEDAY. The two companies will now move into the operational integration phase. Their delivery networks, teams, and internal systems will be gradually aligned to provide customers with a seamless, reliable, and increasingly efficient service that meets the evolving demands of the courier market. “We have reached the finish line of a complex process that required significant effort, discipline, and patience from everyone involved. With the acquisition now completed, SAMEDAY and Cargus are one company building a shared future. The integration phase ahead will require just as much dedication, but our objective remains unchanged: to provide a more efficient delivery infrastructure and a higher standard of service for the benefit of our customers and business partners,” said Lucian Baltaru, CEO of SAMEDAY Group . “The completion of the acquisition by SAMEDAY marks the beginning of a new and important chapter for Cargus. We are joining SAMEDAY with the confidence that, together, we can build a stronger, more efficient network and deliver an even higher standard of service to all our customers. I would like to thank our colleagues at Cargus for their professionalism and commitment throughout this process, and I warmly welcome everyone to the first stage of this shared journey,” said Belgin Bactali, CEO of Cargus . By combining the logistics capabilities and human resources of both companies, SAMEDAY aims to strengthen its nationwide coverage and improve delivery efficiency for both individual customers and business partners. Further details regarding the integration timeline and any impact on customer services will be communicated separately as the integration process progresses. https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/topical-i.text: Prime Minister Robert Fico (Smer-SD) announced on Thursday that he will visit Ukraine on Friday September 18th. He added that he's due to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and new Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, while Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also stated on Thursday that he would meet Fico in Ukraine. The Government Office clarified that the Slovak Prime Minister will travel to Ukraine to attend a conference with the prime ministers of other EU countries. During his visit to Presov, Fico expressed concerns about how the conflict in Ukraine evolves. "The situation has never been as serious and tense in terms of the possibility of a pan-European military conflict as it is now," Fico said, adding that he doesn't want Slovakia to become involved in any war. He made the statement in the context of Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, according to which an armed attack against one NATO member is considered an attack against all members. "Yes, we're part of NATO, we appreciate that, and we are committed to cooperation and meeting our obligations. But as prime minister, I'll do everything I can to ensure that Slovakia is never drawn into an armed conflict," said Fico, expressing his fears that we are "on the brink", while he cannot imagine what would happen in Slovakia if it faced problems arising from a war. "What is happening in Europe today, what we are hearing and seeing, is that the military conflict in Ukraine has spiralled out of control. All rules governing military operations have been abandoned, and civilian infrastructure is coming under attack. I think we'll witness major military operations on Ukrainian territory. But what I fear most is how strong the military rhetoric in Europe has become. It appears that arms companies will emerge as the winners from the EU's 2028–2034 budget. Not citizens, but arms companies," Fico told the students, adding that he's afraid of war. "I hope that tomorrow night, when I return from Ukraine, I will not be as sceptical as I am now. After last week's meeting with the Visegrad Four (V4: the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia) prime ministers in Bratislava, I couldn't sleep that night after listening to what the Polish, Hungarian and Czech prime ministers, as well as the Irish prime minister who attended the meeting as the representative of the country holding the EU Council presidency, had said. I didn't feel good about any of it," said Fico. He also told the students that peace should not be taken for granted. "We have it today, but tomorrow there may be nothing. Let's keep our fingers crossed so that things only get better and that the big boys in politics, as I call them, come to their senses, because sometimes I feel like they're losing track of and control over what's currently happening in the world," remarked Fico. Fico went on to add that he hopes that Slovakia will not be a part of a military conflict just because of some Article 5. He stated that Slovakia is a part of NATO and takes this responsibility very seriously, along with cooperation and fulfilling Slovakia’s obligations. But, as Premier of Slovakia he will do everything he can to ensure that Slovakia is never pulled into a military conflict. Source: TASR

https://www.dw.com/en/a-migrant-boat-san.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O8Lc The UN migration agency IOM has called for donors to help Djibouti's rescue efforts, as Red Sea crossings — and sinkings — increase dramatically Image: Luis Tato/AFP Advertisement The United Nations International Organization for Migration (IOM) on Sunday said that 109 people were killed, 80 survived and 116 remained missing after the overnight sinking of a migrant boat off the coast of Djibouti in northeastern Africa . The vessel, which was estimated to have been carrying 350 people, capsized near Obock, Djibouti, en route to Yemen . In a statement, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac called the loss of life "devastating," adding, "This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities" by trying to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and reach Gulf countries. "Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East," according to the IOM. IOM representatives said, "Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing." Djibouti to Yemen a dangerous crossing The IOM says it has detected more than 20,000 crossings from Djibouti to Yemen — which is currently in the middle of a raging civil war — in the past month. More than 900 migrants were killed attempting the passage in 2025. The IOM says most of those attempting to cross are from Ethiopia and Somalia. The 80 survivors from Saturday night's capsizing were all Ethiopian nationals. The IMO on Sunday urged "donors and partners to strengthen support for Djibouti's response, including search and rescue operations and life-saving assistance." Of the bodies so far recovered, 52 were men, 42 were women and 15 were children. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6wy.text: Figure caption, Watch: BBC at scene as emergency crews head towards Channel Tunnel crash By Patrick Jackson Â and Â Toby Mann Published 15 October 2026 A bus has hit a stationary freight train near the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel, injuring the driver and 18 passengers, French authorities say. The bus, which was carrying lorry drivers due to take a shuttle rail service, struck the train at the loading platform of the tunnel in Coquelles, near Calais, at 19:27 (18:27 BST) on Thursday. The bus driver and one passenger were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter. None of the injuries were life threatening, a local official said. Local sub-prefect Agathe Cury said freight and Eurostar passenger traffic through the tunnel had not been disrupted after a brief stoppage to evacuate injured people. An investigation has begun. Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Trains near the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel (file image) "Two trains were on either side of the platform. One was being loaded by heavy goods vehicles ahead of a cross-Channel journey, and another train that had previously been loaded was departing," Cury said. "For a reason that currently remains unknown, the minibus collided with the departing train. "The bus did not overturn, it is still upright â but the shock and the collision caused injuries to the people involved." The incident involved a minibus transporting workers who were about to board Le Shuttle. All were men of different nationalities, she added. It is not clear whether any British nationals are among the injured. Cury said it was "the first time an incident of this type has occurred" on an Eurotunnel loading platform. The BBC's Evan Davis, who was travelling through the Eurotunnel to Calais at the time of the incident, witnessed blue light vehicles "concentrated on one of the platforms" as he entered France. "There were plenty of cars queueing up at check-in when I drove past just now, and I saw some cars going through check-in, so despite the collision they weren't being held," he said from the scene. Photos published by local French newspaper La Voix du Nord , external showed a small bus with damage to its front and side standing alongside a train, among a crowd of emergency workers. Eurostar has released an update saying: "An incident occurred several kilometers away from the Channel Tunnel. "This incident does not involved or impact Eurostar trains running from and to London. All of Eurostar trains will run as expected." The Eurotunnel runs under the sea between England and France, from Folkestone in Kent to Coquelles on the French side. Three different rail services operate through the tunnel - the Eurostar, a passenger train that begins in London and goes to several European destinations, freight trains which transport goods and Le Shuttle, which transports vehicles.
